title: HIV–TB synergy
dek: HIV is the acquired CD4 knockout that turns contained TB into disseminated, smear-variable, LAM-useful, IRIS-prone disease. The two epidemics amplify each other at every step.
story: HIV depletes CD4 T cells, wrecks granuloma architecture, and multiplies lifetime TB risk from the classical ~5–10% toward an annual risk that can exceed that lifetime figure at low CD4. Incident TB also accelerates HIV progression. This is synergy, not two independent columns on a form.

Disease looks different: more extrapulmonary, more miliary, more smear-negative pulmonary disease with high tissue burden. That is why WHO-recommended rapid molecular tests, urine LF-LAM in advanced HIV, and empiric treatment algorithms exist. IGRA/TST miss more people as anergy sets in.

IRIS — paradoxical worsening after ART as the immune system returns — is the reconstitution tax, especially with TB meningitis and high burden. ART timing is a separate plate; the biology is that CD4 return into an antigen-loaded CNS can be dangerous.
deepTitle: Diagnostics and prevention follow the immunology
deep: LF-LAM (Determine TB LAM Ag) is a lipoarabinomannan antigen test on urine, useful when CD4 is low or the person is seriously ill — exactly when sputum assays fail and burden is high. It is not a community screening test in HIV-negative outpatients.

TPT for people with HIV (3HP, 1HP, 3HR, 6H, with 6Lfx if the exposure is MDR/RR) is among the highest-leverage prevention moves in medicine. Screen for disease first; do not let CXR absence become a barrier in high-burden HIV clinics.

Rifamycin–ART induction (rifampin ≫ rifabutin in some tables; rifapentine still induces) is the pharmacology overlay. Dolutegravir twice daily with rifampin is the common modern patch; protease inhibitors and rifampin are a bad marriage.
CD4 < 100 is a different diagnostic prior than CD4 450. Write the CD4 on the lab slip.

visual.caption: Schematic relative risk and assay behaviour as CD4 falls — not a meta-analysis. Disease risk and LAM yield rise; smear and IGRA yield fall. NAAT stays the front door.

example.title: Smear-negative, LAM-positive, CD4 32
example.setup: Inpatient with HIV, CD4 32, cough, hypoxia. Smear negative, Ultra trace, urine LF-LAM positive.

steps.title: Believe the prior
steps.body: Advanced HIV plus LAM+ is TB until a better explanation. Trace Ultra is concordant paucibacillary sputum, not a veto.

steps.title: Start TB therapy and ART on the HIV/TB clock
steps.body: Pulmonary/disseminated: ART within two weeks. If meningitis is in play, delay ART (see tb-hiv-art).

steps.title: Still culture
steps.body: Need DST. LAM does not grade rpoB.

example.takeaway: HIV changes pretest probability and which assays work — not the need for DST.

check.prompt: In advanced HIV, pulmonary TB is often smear-negative because:
choices: There are never bacilli in the lung
Poorly formed cavities and more disseminated/paucibacillary sputum despite high tissue burden
Xpert cannot be used in HIV
check.answer: Poorly formed cavities and more disseminated/paucibacillary sputum despite high tissue burden
check.why: Smear is a density-in-sputum test, not a body-burden test.

check.prompt: LF-LAM sensitivity rises as CD4 falls. For an inpatient with CD4 32 and TB symptoms, WHO’s use case is closest to:
choices: Adjunctive diagnostic in advanced HIV / seriously ill PLHIV, not a standalone DST
check.answer: Adjunctive diagnostic in advanced HIV / seriously ill PLHIV, not a standalone DST
check.why: LAM is an antigen lateral flow with a CD4-dependent likelihood ratio.

check.prompt: On the small-multiples plate, which assay’s schematic yield rises as CD4 falls?
check.why: Smear bars fall; LAM bars rise. That is the teaching contrast.
